tools.description:
Search official Microsoft/Azure documentation to find the most relevant and trustworthy content for a user's query. This tool returns up to 10 high-quality content chunks (each max 500 tokens), extracted from Microsoft Learn and other official sources. Each result includes the article title, URL, and a self-contained content excerpt optimized for fast retrieval and reasoning. Always use this tool to quickly ground your answers in accurate, first-party Microsoft/Azure knowledge.

## Follow-up Pattern
To ensure completeness, use microsoft_docs_fetch when high-value pages are identified by search. The fetch tool complements search by providing the full detail. This is a required step for comprehensive results.

To get started using Azure OpenAI in your applications, you need to create an Azure OpenAI Service and deploy a model that can be used to perform tasks such as converting natural language to SQL, generating email/SMS message content, and more.
In this exercise you will:
1. Create an Azure OpenAI Service resource.
2. Deploy a model.
3. Update the *.env* file with values from your Azure OpenAI service resource.
![Microsoft Cloud scenario overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-cloud/dev/tutorials/openai-acs-msgraph/media/scenario-overview-no-title.png)
### Create an Azure OpenAI Service Resource
1. Visit the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com) in your browser and sign in.
2. Enter *openai* in the **search bar** at the top of the portal page and select **Azure OpenAI** from the options that appear.
 ![Azure OpenAI Service in the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-cloud/dev/tutorials/openai-acs-msgraph/media/search-openai-portal.png)
3. Select **Create** in the toolbar.
 Note
 While this tutorial focuses on Azure OpenAI, if you have an OpenAI API key and would like to use it, you can skip this section and go directly to the **Update the Project's .env File** section below. Assign your OpenAI API key to `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the *.env* file (you can ignore any other `.env` instructions related to OpenAI).
4. Azure OpenAI models are available in specific regions. Visit the [Azure OpenAI model availability](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/concepts/models?WT.mc_id=m365-94501-dwahlin#global-standard-model-availability) document to learn which regions support the gpt-4o model used in this tutorial.
5. Perform the following tasks:
5.1. Select your Azure subscription.
5.2. Select the resource group to use (create a new one if needed).
5.3. Select a region where the gpt-4o model is supported based on the document you looked at earlier.
5.4. Enter the resource name. It must be a unique value.
5.5. Select the **Standard S0** pricing tier.
6. Select **Next** until you get to the **Review + submit** screen. Select **Create**.
7. content.text:
I found these relevant Microsoft Learn resources for **Azure OpenAI**:

- [Azure OpenAI quickstart](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-foundry/openai/quickstart) — Create a deployment and make your first text-generation calls.
- [Create an Azure OpenAI resource and deploy a model](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-foundry/openai/how-to/create-resource) — Resource and model deployment setup.
- [Azure OpenAI models and regional availability](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-foundry/openai/concepts/models) — Supported models, deployment types, and region availability.
- [Azure AI learning resources](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/ai/resources/azure-ai) — SDKs, samples, references, and training resources.
- [Whisper speech-to-text quickstart](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-foundry/openai/whisper-quickstart) — Audio transcription using Python, TypeScript, and other options.
- [Image-generation quickstart](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/dall-e#quickstart) — Generate images through Azure OpenAI.
- [Tutorial: Create an Azure OpenAI resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-cloud/dev/tutorials/openai-acs-msgraph/02-openai-create-resource) — Guided Azure portal exercise.

The documentation is organized around quickstarts, model deployment, SDK/API usage, authentication, content filtering, quotas, regional availability, RAG, fine-tuning, audio, and image generation.
